requirements.subject: ent:continue-statement
requirements.canonical: The `continue` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Next iteration of a loop; Associated keyword or symbol: continue

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The `log` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Logging; Associated keyword or symbol: log

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: The `alt` statement MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
requirements.original: Statement: Alternative behaviour (see note); Associated keyword or symbol: alt {…}

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: The `repeat` statement MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
requirements.original: Statement: Re-evaluation of alternative behaviour (see note); Associated keyword or symbol: repeat

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The `interleave` statement MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
requirements.original: Statement: Interleaved behaviour (see note); Associated keyword or symbol: interleave {…}

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `activate` operation MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
requirements.original: Statement: Activate a default (see note); Associated keyword or symbol: activate

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `deactivate` operation MAY be used in control behaviour only to control timer operations.
requirements.original: Statement: Deactivate a default (see note); Associated keyword or symbol: deactivate

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer `start` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Start timer; Associated keyword or symbol: start

requirements.subject: ent:stop-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer `stop` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Stop timer; Associated keyword or symbol: stop

requirements.subject: ent:read-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer `read` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Read elapsed time; Associated keyword or symbol: read

requirements.subject: ent:running-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer `running` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Check if timer running; Associated keyword or symbol: running

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-operation
requirements.canonical: The timer `timeout` operation MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Timeout event; Associated keyword or symbol: timeout

requirements.subject: ent:action-statement
requirements.canonical: The `action` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Stimulate an (SUT) action externally; Associated keyword or symbol: action

requirements.subject: ent:execute-statement
requirements.canonical: The `execute` statement MAY be used in control behaviour.
requirements.original: Statement: Execute test case; Associated keyword or symbol: execute

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: The concrete mechanism for stopping all PTCs at MTC termination IS tool specific and outside the scope of the standard.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The concrete mechanism for stopping all PTCs is tool specific and therefore outside the scope of the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:final-verdict
requirements.canonical: The final verdict of a test case IS calculated from the final local verdicts of the test components according to the rules of clause 24.1.
requirements.original: The final verdict of a test case is calculated based on the final local verdicts of the different test components according to the rules defined in clause 24.1.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: The actual local verdict of a test component becomes its final local verdict when the test component terminates itself or is stopped by itself, by another test component or by the test system.
requirements.original: The actual local verdict of a test component becomes its final local verdict when the test component terminates itself or is stopped by itself, another test component or by the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.canonical: The MTC SHOULD ensure, by means of the `done` or `killed` operation, that all PTCs have stopped before it stops itself.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: To avoid race conditions for the calculation of test verdicts due to the delayed stopping of PTCs, the MTC should ensure that all PTCs have stopped (by means of the done or killed statement) before it stops itself.

ambiguity.issue: done and killed are called "statement" although the standard defines them as component operations.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The execution of a test case MAY be supervised by a timer.
requirements.original: Timer may be used to supervise the execution of a test case.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-value
requirements.canonical: Test case supervision IS done by an explicit timeout (TimerValue) in the `execute` statement.
requirements.original: This may be done using an explicit timeout in the execute statement.

ambiguity.issue: "may" can be read as a permission (one possible way, others exist) or as a description of the only mechanism; the execute statement timeout is the only mechanism defined, so the descriptive reading is used.
readings: Test case supervision IS done by an explicit timeout (TimerValue) in the `execute` statement.
Test case supervision MAY be done by an explicit timeout in the `execute` statement or by other means.

requirements.subject: ent:execute-statement
requirements.condition: the test case does not end within the duration given by the TimerValue of the execute statement
requirements.canonical: If the test case does not end within the supervision duration, the result of the `execute` statement SHALL be the verdict `error`.
requirements.original: If the test case does not end within this duration, the result of the test case execution shall be an error verdict and the test system shall terminate the test case.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.condition: the test case does not end within the duration given by the TimerValue of the execute statement
requirements.canonical: If the test case does not end within the supervision duration, the test system SHALL terminate the test case.
requirements.original: If the test case does not end within this duration, the result of the test case execution shall be an error verdict and the test system shall terminate the test case.

requirements.subject: ent:system-timer
requirements.canonical: The timer used for test case supervision IS a system timer.
requirements.original: The timer used for test case supervision is a system timer and need not be declared or started.

requirements.subject: ent:system-timer
requirements.canonical: The test case supervision timer NEED NOT be declared or started.
requirements.original: The timer used for test case supervision is a system timer and need not be declared or started.

requirements.subject: ent:host-id
requirements.condition: a host id is provided in the execute statement
requirements.canonical: If a host id is given in an `execute` statement, the MTC SHALL be started and execute its behaviour on the deployment location identified by the host id.
requirements.original: A host id can be used to give a specific deployment location to the test system where the MTC shall be started and execute its behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:execute-statement
requirements.condition: a host id is provided and the MTC cannot be deployed on the specified host
requirements.canonical: If a host id is provided and the MTC cannot be deployed on the specified host, the `execute` statement SHALL end with a test case error.
requirements.original: If a host id is provided, the execute statement shall end with a test case error if the MTC cannot be deployed on the specified host.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-value
requirements.canonical: The TimerValue of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to a non-negative `float` value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
requirements.original: a) The TimerValue shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).

requirements.subject: ent:timer-value
requirements.canonical: The TimerValue of an `execute` statement SHALL NOT resolve to `infinity` or `not_a_number`.
requirements.original: a) The TimerValue shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the corresponding formal parameter of the test case is not a template parameter
requirements.canonical: If the corresponding formal parameter is not of template kind, an actual parameter (TemplateInstance) of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to an expression.
requirements.original: b) When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type TemplateInstance shall resolve to an _Expression._ c) The execute statement shall not be called from within an existing executing test behaviour chain called from a test case, i.e. test cases can only be executed from a control behaviour.

ambiguity.issue: The grammar symbol TemplateInstance is used where the actual parameter is meant (the syntax block uses ActualPar); "of template type" means a template formal parameter, not a type.

requirements.subject: ent:execute-statement
requirements.canonical: The `execute` statement SHALL NOT be called from within a test behaviour called from a test case; a test case SHALL only be executed from control behaviour.
requirements.original: b) When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type TemplateInstance shall resolve to an _Expression._ c) The execute statement shall not be called from within an existing executing test behaviour chain called from a test case, i.e. test cases can only be executed from a control behaviour.

ambiguity.issue: "executing test behaviour chain" is not a defined term; the call chain of functions and altsteps started by a test case (test behaviour) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:host-id
requirements.canonical: The HostId parameter of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to a `charstring` value.
requirements.original: d) The HostId parameter shall resolve to a charstring value.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The execution of a TTCN-3 test suite IS controlled by the module control function.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 test suite execution is controlled by the module control function.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The module control function defines the order, sequence, loops, preconditions and actual parameters with which test cases are executed.
requirements.original: The module control function defines, in which order, sequence, loop, under which preconditions, and with which parameters test cases are to be executed.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The module control function IS an entry point for the execution of a TTCN-3 test suite.
requirements.original: The module control function is an entry point for execution of a TTCN-3 test suite.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the module control function has formal parameters
requirements.canonical: If the module control function has formal parameters, actual values SHALL be provided for them when the module control function is executed.
requirements.original: If the function contains formal parameters, their actual values shall be provided.

requirements.subject: ent:control-component
requirements.canonical: When the module control function is started, the test system creates a test component called control component.
requirements.original: When the control function is started, the TE creates a test component called control component.

ambiguity.issue: The abbreviation "TE" (TTCN-3 executable) is not defined in the core language; "test system" is the glossary term. "control function" means the module control function.

requirements.subject: ent:control-component
requirements.canonical: The control component contains the variables, constants, templates and timers used to control the execution of the test suite.
requirements.original: The component contains variables, constants, templates and timers important for controlling of the execution of the test suite.

requirements.subject: ent:control-component
requirements.canonical: The control component IS of the component type specified in the `runs on` clause of the module control function.
requirements.original: The created control component is of the type specified in the runs `on clause of the` module control function.

requirements.subject: ent:control-component
requirements.condition: the module control function has no runs on clause
requirements.canonical: If the module control function has no `runs on` clause, an empty control component IS created.
requirements.original: If the runs `on clause is missing, an empty control component is created.`

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: Program statements in the module control function CAN specify the order in which test cases are executed and the number of times a test case runs.
requirements.original: Program statements specify such things like the order in which test cases are to be executed or the number of times a test case should run.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: If no program statements are used, test cases ARE executed by default in the sequential order in which they appear in the module control function.
requirements.original: If no programming statements are used then, by default, the test cases are executed in the sequential order in which they appear in the module control function.

ambiguity.issue: The module control function needs execute statements, so "no programming statements" most likely means no control-flow statements; reading chosen: execute statements without control-flow statements run in textual order.
readings: If the module control function contains no control-flow statements, its `execute` statements ARE executed in textual order.
If the module control function contains no statements other than test case references, the referenced test cases ARE executed in textual order.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool MAY override the default test case execution order to let a user or tool select a different execution order.
requirements.original: NOTE: This does not preclude the possibility that certain tools may wish to override this default ordering to allow a user or tool to select a different execution order.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-operation
requirements.canonical: A timer operation MAY be used explicitly in the module control function to control test case execution.
requirements.original: Timer operations may also be used explicitly to control test case execution.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: Selection and deselection of test cases CAN be used to control the execution of test cases.
requirements.original: The selection and deselection of test cases can also be used to control the execution of test cases.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: A boolean expression MAY be used in the module control function to select or deselect test cases for execution.
requirements.original: For example, boolean expressions may be used to select and deselect which test cases are to be executed.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function returning a `boolean` value MAY be used in the module control function to select or deselect test cases for execution.
requirements.original: This includes, of course, the use of functions that return a boolean value.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: Test cases MAY be executed as a group by collecting their `execute` statements in a function that is invoked from the module control function.
requirements.original: Another way to execute test cases as a group is to collect them in a control function and invoke that function from the module control function.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The module control function CAN make the order of test case execution depend on the `verdicttype` value returned by a test case.
requirements.original: As a test case returns a single value of type verdicttype, it is also possible to control the order of test case execution depending on the outcome of a test case.

requirements.subject: ent:verdicttype
requirements.canonical: A `verdicttype` value returned by an `execute` statement MAY be used to select test cases for execution.
requirements.original: The use of the TTCN-3 verdicttype is another way to select test cases.

introduces the restrictions list; refers to general static rules in clause 5 and table 16
